name: LM2596S adjustable buck module
description: Ubiquitous 43×21 mm LM2596S adjustable buck board, up to 40 V in and 1.25–35 V out, for quick bench and hobby supplies.

variants.note: ProtoSupplies SKU; the same board is sold by many vendors

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Advertised 3 A, but about 1.5 A continuous (2 A peak) without a heatsink.
Stores list 3.5 V minimum input; the LM2596 itself is rated from 4.5 V.
High output ripple (50–400 mV); add filtering for analog/sensor rails.

terminals.name: IN+
terminals.note: Input voltage, 3.5-40 V per the vendor page.

terminals.name: OUT-
terminals.note: Output ground, common with IN- (not isolated).

adjust.direction: clockwise raises Vout; counter-clockwise lowers Vout

notes: Set the output voltage before connecting a load. Modules µsually ship with the pot turned fully clockwise, so the output is close to VIN. It takes several counter-clockwise turns before the output starts to drop.
With the silkscreen upright, input is on the left end and output on the right end. The vendor text does not say which of IN+ and IN- (or OUT+ and OUT-) is on top.
Solder pads are not on a 0.1 in pitch, so the module does not plug into a breadboard. Two holes for M3 mounting screws.
The output can be set no higher than about VIN - 1.5 V (e.g. about 10.5 V from 12 V in). The load condition is not stated.
Rated 1.5 A continuous, 2 A short-term, 24 W maximum. The vendor does not recommend more than about 1.5 A long-term because the IC, capacitors and inductor get hot.
Output ripple averages about 300 mV (50-400 mV depending on load). The vendor suggests an extra output filter capacitor to reduce it and says the output is not ideal for driving logic directly.
The IC has built-in over-current and thermal limiting. Reverse-polarity protection is not mentioned.
Switching frequency is 150 kHz. Measured efficiency is 66-86%.
Wire the input and output before applying power. Components get hot under heavy load.
